questions.question: Phase charge in electrical stimulation is determined by:

options.A: Pulse amplitude multiplied by pulse duration

questions.explanation: Higher phase charge recruits more nerve fibres; it is a key determinant of comfort and recruitment.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; Kitchen, Electrotherapy: Evidence-Based Practice (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: According to the strength–duration relationship, as the pulse duration is shortened the intensity needed to reach threshold:
questions.explanation: Short pulses need high intensity; long pulses need low intensity (rheobase).
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; Kitchen, Electrotherapy: Evidence-Based Practice (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: A pulse with a very rapid rise to peak and rapid fall is described as:
questions.explanation: Rapid rise time causes accommodation of nerve less than slow rise.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; Kitchen, Electrotherapy: Evidence-Based Practice (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Increasing the pulse repetition rate while keeping pulse width unchanged will:

options.A: Increase the average current and the frequency of muscle contraction

questions.explanation: Average current = amplitude × duration × frequency.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; Kitchen, Electrotherapy: Evidence-Based Practice (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: In a surged current, the amplitude of successive pulses:

options.B: Gradually increases and decreases, producing a ramp contraction

questions.explanation: Surging mimics voluntary muscle contraction.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; Kitchen, Electrotherapy: Evidence-Based Practice (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Reciprocal stimulation (alternating channels) is used to:

options.D: Stimulate agonist and antagonist alternately, for example in re-education of antagonistic pairs

questions.explanation: Used in spasticity management and functional movement.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; Kitchen, Electrotherapy: Evidence-Based Practice (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Electrical stimulation of the common peroneal nerve during swing is used in:
questions.explanation: Triggered by a heel switch (functional electrical stimulation).
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; Kitchen, Electrotherapy: Evidence-Based Practice (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Electrical muscle stimulation after knee surgery is primarily used to:

options.B: Maintain or restore quadriceps strength and prevent arthrogenic muscle inhibition

questions.explanation: Used with exercise rather than instead of it.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; Kitchen, Electrotherapy: Evidence-Based Practice (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Electrical stimulation in acute Bell's palsy is generally:

options.A: Not recommended in the early stage (insufficient evidence and risk of synkinesis)

questions.explanation: Gentle facial exercises are preferred.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; Kitchen, Electrotherapy: Evidence-Based Practice (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: TENS in chronic neuropathic pain is applied preferably:

options.C: Over the nerve proximal to the painful area or at the dermatome

questions.explanation: Sensory stimulation requires intact sensation.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; Kitchen, Electrotherapy: Evidence-Based Practice (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: In labour, TENS electrodes are commonly placed:

options.D: Over the lower back at T10–L1 and S2–S4

questions.explanation: Provides analgesia in the first stage.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; Kitchen, Electrotherapy: Evidence-Based Practice (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Electrical stimulation of the antagonist to a spastic muscle is used because it:

options.B: Produces reciprocal inhibition of the spastic agonist

questions.explanation: Also strengthens the weak antagonist.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; Kitchen, Electrotherapy: Evidence-Based Practice (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Kots' Russian stimulation uses a burst duration of:

options.B: 10 ms with a 10 ms gap (50% duty cycle)

questions.explanation: At 50 bursts per second.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; Kitchen, Electrotherapy: Evidence-Based Practice (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: A medium-frequency current passes through skin with less discomfort than a low-frequency current mainly because:

options.C: The skin impedance is lower at higher frequency

questions.explanation: Capacitive reactance falls as frequency rises.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; Kitchen, Electrotherapy: Evidence-Based Practice (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: If two interferential currents have frequencies of 4000 Hz and 4100 Hz, the beat frequency produced is:
questions.explanation: Beat frequency = difference of the two frequencies.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; Kitchen, Electrotherapy: Evidence-Based Practice (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Amplitude modulated frequency (AMF) in IFT is the:

options.C: Frequency at which the amplitude of the resultant current varies

questions.explanation: Equal to the beat frequency.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; Kitchen, Electrotherapy: Evidence-Based Practice (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Interferential current should NOT be applied:

options.C: Over the abdomen in pregnancy or over a pacemaker

questions.explanation: Also over thrombosis and malignancy.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; Kitchen, Electrotherapy: Evidence-Based Practice (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: IFT can be used for muscle stimulation by selecting an amplitude modulation frequency of:
questions.explanation: Lower frequencies cause twitches or tetanic contractions.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; Kitchen, Electrotherapy: Evidence-Based Practice (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Shortwave diathermy can raise tissue temperature to a depth of about:

options.A: 3–5 cm in the capacitor-field technique with fat layers considered

questions.explanation: Depth depends on the technique and tissue impedance.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; Kitchen, Electrotherapy: Evidence-Based Practice (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The inductive method of SWD is also called:
questions.explanation: Uses a coil or drum applicator.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; Kitchen, Electrotherapy: Evidence-Based Practice (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The drum (monode) electrode in SWD is an example of:
questions.explanation: The coil in the drum creates the magnetic field.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; Kitchen, Electrotherapy: Evidence-Based Practice (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Why should the skin and dressings be dry when applying SWD?

options.A: Moisture concentrates the field and can cause burns

questions.explanation: Remove wet dressings and sweat; towels should cover the skin.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; Kitchen, Electrotherapy: Evidence-Based Practice (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Before SWD the therapist should ensure the patient:

options.B: Removes metal objects such as jewellery and watches from the field
options.D: Keeps the phone on the skin

questions.explanation: Metal concentrates energy and can burn.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; Kitchen, Electrotherapy: Evidence-Based Practice (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Pulsed shortwave therapy is preferred in:

options.D: Acute soft tissue injury and oedema

questions.explanation: Non-thermal effect with low mean power.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; Kitchen, Electrotherapy: Evidence-Based Practice (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The microwave director is held at a distance of about:
questions.explanation: Intensity decreases with distance (inverse square law).
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; Kitchen, Electrotherapy: Evidence-Based Practice (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Moist dressings must be removed before microwave diathermy because:

options.D: Water absorbs microwaves strongly and may cause burns

questions.explanation: Dry towels are used.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; Kitchen, Electrotherapy: Evidence-Based Practice (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Which of the following has the highest frequency?
questions.explanation: Infrared and UV have even higher frequencies (as light).
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; Kitchen, Electrotherapy: Evidence-Based Practice (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Modern ultrasound transducers use a crystal of:
questions.explanation: Quartz and barium titanate were used earlier.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; Kitchen, Electrotherapy: Evidence-Based Practice (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The ideal coupling medium for ultrasound is one that:

options.D: Has an acoustic impedance similar to skin and transmits a high proportion of energy

questions.explanation: Water-based gels transmit about 70–90%.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; Kitchen, Electrotherapy: Evidence-Based Practice (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: In acute injury, ultrasound dose should be:

options.B: Low intensity, pulsed, for short duration

questions.explanation: Thermal effects would worsen inflammation.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; Kitchen, Electrotherapy: Evidence-Based Practice (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Therapeutic ultrasound should not be applied to:

options.A: The ankle of a pregnant woman
options.D: The abdomen or lumbar region of a pregnant woman

questions.explanation: Fetal exposure is a concern.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; Kitchen, Electrotherapy: Evidence-Based Practice (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Over the growing epiphyses of children, ultrasound should be:

options.A: Avoided or used with caution at low intensity

questions.explanation: Possible damage to growth plates.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; Kitchen, Electrotherapy: Evidence-Based Practice (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Therapeutic ultrasound over metal implants is generally:

options.B: Possible with a moving technique at low intensity, but not over cemented plastic or pacemaker leads

questions.explanation: Metal reflects energy and may heat the implant surface.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; Kitchen, Electrotherapy: Evidence-Based Practice (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The wavelength of ultrasound in tissue is approximately:
questions.explanation: At 1 MHz the wavelength is about 1.5 mm.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; Kitchen, Electrotherapy: Evidence-Based Practice (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Which topical drug is commonly used in phonophoresis?
questions.explanation: Penetration is limited and evidence is modest.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; Kitchen, Electrotherapy: Evidence-Based Practice (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The dosage of infrared radiation is governed mainly by:

options.B: The patient's perception of mild warmth, distance and duration

questions.explanation: Treatment time 10–15 minutes.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; Kitchen, Electrotherapy: Evidence-Based Practice (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Infrared radiation should NOT be applied to:

options.D: Areas of impaired sensation or the eyes, and over arterial insufficiency

questions.explanation: Use eye protection for the face.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; Kitchen, Electrotherapy: Evidence-Based Practice (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Luminous IR generators emit mainly radiation of wavelength:

options.B: Short IR (about 770–1500 nm) with visible light

questions.explanation: Penetrates to the dermis and subcutaneous tissue.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; Kitchen, Electrotherapy: Evidence-Based Practice (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Before UV treatment a test dose is given to determine the:
questions.explanation: Test on the forearm or trunk.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; Kitchen, Electrotherapy: Evidence-Based Practice (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The commonly used test area for the UV sensitivity test is the:
questions.explanation: Choose an area comparable in pigmentation to the treated skin.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; Kitchen, Electrotherapy: Evidence-Based Practice (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: For repeated UV treatments to maintain the same reaction, the dose is usually increased by about:
questions.explanation: To overcome tolerance.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; Kitchen, Electrotherapy: Evidence-Based Practice (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: If the UV lamp is moved from 50 cm to 100 cm, the intensity falls to:
questions.explanation: Inverse square law.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; Kitchen, Electrotherapy: Evidence-Based Practice (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Phototherapy for neonatal jaundice uses light of wavelength about:
questions.explanation: Converts bilirubin to water-soluble isomers.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; Kitchen, Electrotherapy: Evidence-Based Practice (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: PUVA therapy is also used for:
questions.explanation: Photochemotherapy.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; Kitchen, Electrotherapy: Evidence-Based Practice (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Cold relieves pain mainly by:

options.D: Reducing nerve conduction and acting as a counter-irritant (gate control)

questions.explanation: Also reduces inflammation.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; Kitchen, Electrotherapy: Evidence-Based Practice (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The skin temperature at which tissue freezing occurs is below about:
questions.explanation: Do not apply ice directly to the skin for prolonged periods.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; Kitchen, Electrotherapy: Evidence-Based Practice (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Combined cold and compression (e.g. Cryocuff) is more effective than ice alone because:
questions.explanation: Standard in acute sprain management.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; Kitchen, Electrotherapy: Evidence-Based Practice (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The reduction in spasticity following cold application lasts about:
questions.explanation: Used as a window for exercise.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; Kitchen, Electrotherapy: Evidence-Based Practice (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: A whirlpool bath at neutral warm temperature for the foot should be avoided in a:

options.A: Patient with acute oedema or impaired circulation in a dependent position
options.C: Subacute ankle sprain with good circulation

questions.explanation: Dependency increases oedema.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; Kitchen, Electrotherapy: Evidence-Based Practice (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Which immersion depth reduces body weight bearing the most?
questions.explanation: Neck immersion unloads about 90%.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; Kitchen, Electrotherapy: Evidence-Based Practice (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Water temperature in a therapeutic exercise pool is typically:
questions.explanation: Higher (about 36–38 °C) for arthritis or paediatric neurology.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; Kitchen, Electrotherapy: Evidence-Based Practice (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Patients with which condition should not use the hydrotherapy pool?

options.D: Open wounds, infection, fever and incontinence

questions.explanation: Also uncontrolled epilepsy and unstable heart conditions.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; Kitchen, Electrotherapy: Evidence-Based Practice (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: A typical intermittent mechanical lumbar traction session lasts:
questions.explanation: Hold:rest ratios of about 1:1 to 3:1.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; Kitchen, Electrotherapy: Evidence-Based Practice (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: An initial cervical traction force in sitting is usually about:
questions.explanation: Gradually increase as tolerated.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; Kitchen, Electrotherapy: Evidence-Based Practice (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: If a patient reports dizziness or visual disturbance during cervical traction the therapist should:
questions.explanation: Possible vertebrobasilar insufficiency.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; Kitchen, Electrotherapy: Evidence-Based Practice (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Peripheralisation of leg pain during lumbar traction indicates that the traction should be:
questions.explanation: Centralisation is a favourable sign.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; Kitchen, Electrotherapy: Evidence-Based Practice (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: In lumbar traction, a positive effect on disc protrusion is thought to arise from:

options.A: Reduced intradiscal pressure and tension in the posterior longitudinal ligament

questions.explanation: Evidence for traction effectiveness is limited.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; Kitchen, Electrotherapy: Evidence-Based Practice (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: A chronaxie of more than 10 ms in a muscle suggests:
questions.explanation: Normal chronaxie is less than 1 ms.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; Kitchen, Electrotherapy: Evidence-Based Practice (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The accommodation quotient is the ratio of the current needed for a triangular pulse to that for a:

options.C: Rectangular pulse of the same duration

questions.explanation: A value of more than 3 indicates normal accommodation.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; Kitchen, Electrotherapy: Evidence-Based Practice (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Slowing of nerve conduction velocity is characteristic of:
questions.explanation: Amplitude falls in axonal loss.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; Kitchen, Electrotherapy: Evidence-Based Practice (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The F-wave on nerve conduction study is useful to assess:
questions.explanation: It is a late response from antidromic activation.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; Kitchen, Electrotherapy: Evidence-Based Practice (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Normal muscle at complete rest on EMG shows:
questions.explanation: Insertion activity should cease within 300 ms.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; Kitchen, Electrotherapy: Evidence-Based Practice (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Fasciculation potentials are typically seen in:

options.B: Motor neuron disease and lower motor neurone irritability

questions.explanation: They reflect spontaneous firing of a motor unit.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; Kitchen, Electrotherapy: Evidence-Based Practice (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: A ‘dive-bomber’ sound on EMG is characteristic of:
questions.explanation: Seen in myotonic dystrophy.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; Kitchen, Electrotherapy: Evidence-Based Practice (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The H-reflex is the electrical equivalent of the:
questions.explanation: Elicited from the tibial nerve at the popliteal fossa.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; Kitchen, Electrotherapy: Evidence-Based Practice (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: In carpal tunnel syndrome, nerve conduction studies show:

options.B: Prolonged median distal motor and sensory latencies

questions.explanation: The most sensitive test is sensory latency.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; Kitchen, Electrotherapy: Evidence-Based Practice (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: In order of increasing frequency the electromagnetic spectrum includes:
questions.explanation: Wavelength decreases as frequency increases.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; Kitchen, Electrotherapy: Evidence-Based Practice (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The energy of a photon is proportional to its:
questions.explanation: E = hf; UV photons carry more energy than IR.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; Kitchen, Electrotherapy: Evidence-Based Practice (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: When light passes from air into a denser medium it:

options.B: Bends towards the normal and slows down

questions.explanation: Snell's law.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; Kitchen, Electrotherapy: Evidence-Based Practice (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The law of reflection states that:

options.A: The angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection
options.B: Reflection is zero for smooth surfaces

questions.explanation: Mirrors reflect nearly all incident light.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; Kitchen, Electrotherapy: Evidence-Based Practice (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Ultrasound differs from electromagnetic radiation in that it:

options.B: Is a mechanical (acoustic) wave requiring a medium

questions.explanation: Sound cannot travel through a vacuum.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; Kitchen, Electrotherapy: Evidence-Based Practice (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The unit of heat energy in the SI system is the:
questions.explanation: 1 calorie = 4.18 joules.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; Kitchen, Electrotherapy: Evidence-Based Practice (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The specific heat of a substance is the heat required to:

options.B: Raise 1 kg of the substance by 1 °C

questions.explanation: Water has a high specific heat.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; Kitchen, Electrotherapy: Evidence-Based Practice (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Heat always flows from a region of:
questions.explanation: Second law of thermodynamics.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; Kitchen, Electrotherapy: Evidence-Based Practice (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
